vs
Government of Bangladesh and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 12. When the SIA was placed before this Court there was no assertion by the appellant that he had elected for the previous service rules. The appellant's contentions that he was commissioned on 1 April 1954 when the British India Army Act, 1911 (Act No VIII of 1911) and the India Army (Application of Provisions) Act 1950 (Act No. LXXV of 1950) were applicable and they continue to be so applicable in this case under Articles 62,150 and 152 of the Constitution, the impugned order is violative of the still applicable provisions in Rule 12(3) the Indian Army Act and Article 31 of the Constitution are far-fetched and have got no force. Under the above provisions of the SAI the appellant who completed 27 years' of service on the effective list was liable to be compulsorily retired. On 1 August 1983 an order was passed to that effect. But there was an error in that order. Instead of Section 18 of the Army Act, Section 16 was wrongly mentioned in that order.
